facts.label: Present perfect com just, already, yet
facts.sub: Use have + particípio com just, already, yet e ever para ligar o passado ao presente.

facts.label: acabei de…
facts.sub: Use have just + particípio para algo que aconteceu agora há pouco: I’ve just joined a club. Just vem entre have e o particípio.

facts.label: já…
facts.sub: Use already para algo que já aconteceu, às vezes antes do esperado: I’ve already finished half of it. Já vem antes do particípio.

compare.br: No Brasil, dizemos “acabei de entrar” e “nunca li”.
compare.us: Em inglês, use have/has + particípio: I’ve just joined, I’ve never read it. Just, already, yet e ever vão junto do verbo (yet vai no fim). Com ontem ou ano passado, use o passado simples.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: I’ve just joined means I joined a short time ago.

items.why: With yesterday we use the past simple: I joined yesterday.

items.s: Have you ever…? asks about your life up to now.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: I’ve just joined means I joined a short time ago. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We say “I have joined yesterday.” → Falso (With yesterday we use the past simple: I joined yesterday.)
Have you ever…? asks about your life up to now. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: A library in London · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a rainy afternoon in London. Nina walks into a big old library. Ruth works at the desk near the door. There is a shelf of new books behind her. Nina has a new hobby. She wants to meet other readers.

“Hello! Have you just joined the library? I haven’t seen you before.” says Ruth. “Yes, I’ve just joined a book club. We meet here today.” says Nina. “Oh, nice! I’ve been a member of this club for two years.” says Ruth.
